title: Planar operation coherence with specified projection pullbacks
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, transformations, and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the nonsymmetric monoidal convention of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], and the infinity category $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ of infinity categories together with cocartesian straightening and unstraightening over $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], in fixed universes with an auxiliary universe for categories of categories. A unital planar operation system on an infinity category $A$ consists of functors $t_r:A^r\to A$ for $r\geq0$, with $A^0=*$ and $t_1\simeq\mathrm{id}_A$, and homotopy coherent substitution equivalences
$$t_k(t_{r_1},\ldots,t_{r_k})\simeq t_{r_1+\cdots+r_k}.$$
Here the inputs to the $t_{r_i}$ are consecutive disjoint lists, and the coherences mean all equivalences and higher compatibility simplices indexed by finite planar rooted trees, contractions of inner edges, grafting, and insertion or removal of unary identity vertices. Nullary vertices are allowed and specify the unit; an $r$-input tree uses each of its $r$ ordered external inputs exactly once. Every coherence for an $r$-input tree is a transformation, or higher simplex of transformations, between functors $A^r\to A$, before any unused external variables are added. Compatibility with grafting is included as part of these data.

Monoidal infinity categories with underlying category $A$ can be encoded, up to equivalence over $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$, by such unital planar operation systems. Their classifying diagrams admit the following coherent normal form. The fiber at $[n]$ is $A^n$. For $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, put $a=\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}:[m]\to[n]$; the $i$th output of its transport is $t_{a(i)-a(i-1)}$ on the consecutive input list $a(i-1)+1,\ldots,a(i)$, pulled back along that coordinate projection. For any chain of base arrows and a chosen final output, retain just the rooted planar tree of intermediate operations feeding that output. The entire substitution comparison and each of its higher compatibilities is the pullback of the corresponding coherence of this tree along the projection onto its ordered external input list. This is specified projection-pullback data, compatible with all faces, degeneracies, and further block substitutions, not merely a claim that the two endpoint functors happen to factor through a projection. It includes an empty external list, with domain $*$.

Conversely a unital planar operation system gives a coherent normal-form diagram $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ by these formulas. Under cocartesian unstraightening it is a monoidal infinity category in the stated convention. A functor $f:A\to B$, with coherent equivalences $f t_r\simeq u_r f^r$ compatible with the entire planar substitution system, induces a coherent transformation of these diagrams with component $f^n$, hence a functor of their unstraightenings preserving all cocartesian edges. No limits or colimits of $A$ or $B$ are assumed. No full-faithfulness assertion about precomposition along a coordinate projection is made.

source.place: Sections 2.4.1-2.4.2 (cartesian structures and monoid objects: a map in the cartesian structure over a map of finite index sets is the tuple of its components on the preimage blocks, which is the projection-pullback form stated here) and sections 4.1.2-4.1.3: Construction 4.1.2.9 (Cut), Proposition 4.1.2.11, Theorem 4.1.3.14 and Proposition 4.1.3.19; planar active-operation/inert-projection normal form, here formulated explicitly with all projection-pullback coherence data by the agent. The source is not archived in literature; WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical coherence result.

proof.text: Let $p:X\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ be a monoidal infinity category and $A=X_{[1]}$. Straighten $p$ to $F$. The inert transport equivalences in the definition say exactly that $F([n])\to A^n$ is a Segal product cone, including $F([0])\simeq *$. Conversely the unstraightening of any such Segal diagram satisfies also the relative-limit clause of the stated monoidal convention: for $d\in F([m])$, $x\in F([n])$ and $\phi:[m]\to[n]$, cocartesian transport identifies the mapping space over $\phi$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{F([n])}(F(\phi)d,x)$. Under the product equivalence this is $\prod_i\operatorname{Map}_A(F(\rho_i\phi)d,x_i)$, precisely the required relative-limit map. This mapping-space formula is obtained by taking the fiber over $\phi$ in the cocartesian mapping square in the straightening statement. When $n=0$ the product is contractible. Thus this convention and Segal classifying diagrams encode the same objects.

source.place: Definition 4.1.2.5 and the cocartesian/Segal interpretation; the relative-limit verification is written here.

proof.text: The straightening statement supplies finite products in $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$. Form its cartesian structure in the product-diagram model $P\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ of [lem-coef-cartesian-envelope-product-diagram-recognition], which is the model fixed in [lem-coef-cartesian-associative-segal-comparison], and the pullback $q:E^\otimes\to N(\mathsf{Ass}^\otimes)$ described there, where $\mathsf{Ass}$ has one operation for each ordering of a labeled input set. Cocartesian lifts pull back from the cocartesian fibration $P\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$. Its fibers are powers of $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ via the inert projections, its inert maps are projections, and its operation transports are products in the prescribed input order, by the singleton-restriction equivalences, the transport formula and the block mapping-space formula of [lem-coef-cartesian-envelope-product-diagram-recognition]; these are the same formulas as for the cartesian structure of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope]. The block mapping-space formula of the product-diagram model, applied over each ordered pointed map, is exactly the output Segal axiom; hence this pullback is a map of infinity-operads and meets the hypotheses of the reconstruction theorem. The comparison sends $F$ to an inert-preserving section $s$ of $q$. Apply [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction] to this ordinary symmetric operad and $q$. Its color object is $A$. For the standard order on $r$ inputs, its structure arrow is $t_r:A^r\to A$, with all the stated tree contraction, grafting, identity and nullary data. These are functors, and their coherence paths are natural equivalences: [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration] models $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ by cores of functor categories, and [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] identifies these enriched mapping spaces with the intrinsic ones. All these products are ambient products of categories; no product in $A$ is assumed.

source.place: HA 2.4.2.5 and 4.1.2.10; the cited existing reconstruction theorem applied to the ordinary associative operad.

proof.text: Conversely extend the supplied planar system to the ordered operations of $\mathsf{Ass}$. On an input set ordered as $i_1,\ldots,i_r$, use $t_r$ after reindexing the product factors into this order. For a tree labeled by such orders, order its external leaves recursively by the input order at every vertex and use the given planar coherence on that ordered list, precomposed with its reindexing map. A contraction replaces ordered lists by their concatenation; thus it gives the same leaf ordering before and after contraction. Grafting also concatenates the same lists. Relabeling inputs only composes the reindexing maps, and a unary identity inserts the singleton list. These equalities of coordinate maps show that all permutation, contraction, grafting and identity compatibility diagrams, including their higher simplices, are the given planar diagrams pulled back by a fixed reindexing. The empty list uses $t_0$. Hence these data meet every hypothesis of [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction] for the $q$ of step 2. Its reconstruction equivalence gives an inert-preserving section $s$ with the specified data and all their parameter families. Its unary operation is identified with the identity, as required by that theorem; an initial specified $t_1\simeq\mathrm{id}_A$ is retained in this identification. Applying the cartesian associative--Segal comparison gives a Segal diagram $H$. We now identify this particular diagram's complete block and higher-simplex formulas.

source.place: Apply the existing outputwise section reconstruction to the symmetric associative operad, then HA 2.4.2.5 and 4.1.2.10; explicit ordered-list extension is written here.

proof.text: Set $G([n])=A^n$. For $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ and $a=\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}$, write $I_i=\{a(i-1)+1,\ldots,a(i)\}$. Define the $i$th component of $G(\alpha)$ to be $t_{|I_i|}\operatorname{pr}_{I_i}$. The $I_i$ are disjoint consecutive lists; the entries outside $(a(0),a(m)]$ are discarded. For a second arrow $\beta:[m]\to[\ell]$, with opposite $b$, the $j$th composite component applies $t_{b(j)-b(j-1)}$ to the outputs with $b(j-1)<i\leq b(j)$. Their external inputs concatenate, in order, to $\{a(b(j-1))+1,\ldots,a(b(j))\}$. Its length is the telescoping sum $\sum_i(a(i)-a(i-1))=a(b(j))-a(b(j-1))$. Pull back the specified substitution equivalence on that ordered input list along its projection from $A^n$. This defines the comparison with $G(\beta\alpha)$; for an empty list it is pulled back along $A^n\to *$.

source.place: Construction 4.1.2.9, block formula; explicit interval calculation from the given operation system.

proof.text:
Let $\pi$ be the coherent product-evaluation functor of [lem-coef-cartesian-envelope-product-diagram-recognition] and define $G=\pi sN(\operatorname{Cut})$, using the Cut functor of [lem-coef-cartesian-associative-segal-comparison]. This is a coherent diagram by composition, with $G([n])=A^n$ under the specified product cones. Apply [lem-coef-cut-chain-forest-compatibility] to a chain and a chosen final output $j$. It identifies the retained planar tree, its ordered external interval $L_j$, and all contractions, endpoint restrictions, unary insertions and graftings, including empty lists. For endpoint faces use its full forest record before pruning.

By the forest clause of [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction], the complete section-coherence simplex is the product of the supplied output-tree simplices pulled back along their external-input projections. By the evaluation and simplicial-operator formulas of [lem-coef-cartesian-envelope-product-diagram-recognition], applying $\pi$ evaluates this product as the tuple of the tree simplices precomposed with $\operatorname{pr}_{L_j}:A^{n_0}\to A^{|L_j|}$. This applies to entire parameter simplices. The arbitrary-parameter and restriction clauses of reconstruction, together with the cited forest compatibility, identify their faces, degeneracies and further substitutions with those of $G$. Hence these are its full specified projection-pullback coherences.

source.place: HA Construction 4.1.2.9 and sections 2.4.1-2.4.2; finite-forest indexing extracted as lem-coef-cut-chain-forest-compatibility, and complete parameter-simplex evaluation supplied by the existing reconstruction and product-diagram recognition statements.

proof.text: The preceding definition of $G$ is exactly the comparison functor of [lem-coef-cartesian-associative-segal-comparison] applied to the reconstructed section $s$: that functor is the specified composition with $N(\operatorname{Cut})$ and $\pi$. Consequently $G\simeq H$ as complete diagrams. For an inert arrow every block is a singleton, so step 4 gives the coordinate projection followed by the specified unary identity equivalence; the inert maps exhibit the Segal product cones. If the planar system came from the original $F$, the ordered-list extension in step 3 recovers the section data of step 2: an operation of $\mathsf{Ass}$ with any input order is the standard-order operation composed with its input permutation, and the section's permutation compatibilities identify precisely these reindexings, including their full tree diagrams. The restriction/reconstruction equivalence, not merely equality of the arity maps, therefore identifies the reconstructed section with the original section. Applying the comparison gives $G\simeq F$. Straightening sends this coherent diagram equivalence to an equivalence of total categories over $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$.

source.place: The specified comparison functor of HA 2.4.2.5 and 4.1.2.10 on the full reconstructed section, followed by straightening.

proof.text: Unstraighten $G$. Its fibers are $A^n$ and its transports are the block formulas by the straightening equivalence. Its inert maps are the coordinate projections up to the specified unary identity equivalence. The mapping-space computation of step 1 verifies the relative-limit clause, so its total category is monoidal in the exact convention used by the item, including the empty fiber product at $[0]$.

source.place: Cocartesian straightening with the defining Segal conditions; relative-limit check in step 1.

proof.text: Let $f:A\to B$ have the specified coherent operation equivalences $ft_r\simeq u_rf^r$ and all their planar tree compatibilities. Extend them to ordered labeled inputs by the reindexings of step 3: $\operatorname{pr}_{I}f^n=f^{|I|}\operatorname{pr}_{I}$, so these reindexings commute with $f$ and compose identically on every compatibility simplex. Apply the transformation and arbitrary-parameter clauses of [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction] to obtain a coherent transformation of the two reconstructed sections of the same $q$. Its component on a tuple of $n$ colors is the tuple of $n$ copies of $f$. Postcompose with $\pi$ and restrict along $N(\operatorname{Cut})$. These are functors on the entire section/diagram categories, so they give a transformation of the particular diagrams $G_A\to G_B$ from step 5, with all higher families; the comparison also identifies it as the image of the given algebra morphism. Its degree-$n$ component is $f^n$. On a block $I$ its naturality equivalence is $ft_{|I|}\simeq u_{|I|}f^{|I|}$ pulled back along $\operatorname{pr}_{I}$. On a chain its full naturality diagram is the given tree-compatible family on the retained ordered tree, pulled back along the same projection as in step 5, by the reconstruction theorem's forest and parameter clauses. Finally straightening sends this transformation to a functor of total categories preserving all cocartesian edges. No map between endomorphism operads of different colors is used.

source.place: Existing coherent section reconstruction on transformations and arbitrary parameters; HA cartesian algebra--monoid/Cut comparison, then cocartesian straightening.

proof.text: All nullary cases were included: a block of length zero uses $t_0$ and the unique projection to $*$; an arrow with target $[0]$ has no output components; a chain passing through $[0]$ uses only unit trees thereafter. A unit can exist only if $A$ has an object, so the argument asserts no unital structure on an empty category. Finite products have been taken in $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$, never in $A$ or $B$; no limit or colimit of $A$ or $B$ entered the construction. The projection formulas specify the simplices themselves and do not require or assert full faithfulness of precomposition with any projection.
